title: Zero Acceptance Probability Without a Perfect Matching
statement: Let $n,k,m$ be natural numbers, let $R$ be a commutative ring with decidable equality, and let $A$ be a Boolean matrix indexed by $\text{Fin}(n)\times\text{Fin}(n)$. If the bipartite graph specified by $A$ has no perfect matching, then the probability, for a uniformly chosen $m$-bit string, that the determinant of the adjacency-masked matrix of sampled entries over $R$ is nonzero is zero.
hypotheses_covered: The graph specified by $A$ has no perfect matching
